newsitem.title: UK: UK wheat, barley stocks rise by end 1995/96.
newsitem.headline: UK wheat, barley stocks rise by end 1995/96.

text.p: Final supply and demand figures for UK cereals in the 1995/96 season suggested a sharp increase in both wheat and barley stocks, the Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) said on Tuesday.
Data compiled by the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (MAFF) showed that some 753,000 tonnes of wheat was held on farm, more than three times that of the previous season.
This confirmed the view that large stocks of wheat and barley were kept on farm as producers held onto supplies in anticipation of higher prices and a delay in the 1996 harvest.
Total wheat stocks at the end of last season were 1.35 million tonnes, excluding stocks held in Scotland on farm, against 755,000 tonnes in the 1994/95 season.
Barley stocks totalled 743,000 tonnes last season.

The usage of wheat by human and industrial processors showed an increase of 2.4 percent or 136,000 tonnes in the 1995/96 season tonnes while animal feed processors used four percent or 153,000 tonnes less wheat.
Distillers' consumption of barley was up six percent or 115,000 tonnes while the usage for animal feed was 1.15 million tonnes, representing an increase of 54 percent.
The swing from wheat to barley in animal feed was attributed to a significant price discount for barley against wheat for most of the season. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 8072
